question: Should Oracle core expose authenticated Codex security-finding actions that can create PRs, start chats, close findings, and adjust findings once the mechanical blockers are fixed?
rationale: Code review can assess postconditions and confirmation safeguards, but it cannot decide whether this authenticated mutation surface belongs in Oracle’s core CLI.

options.title: Sponsor read-only discovery first
options.body: Land only listing and report extraction now, while deferring mutating action commands until their browser contract and ownership are explicitly accepted.

options.title: Sponsor the full action workflow
options.body: Accept the operational commands after the findings below are fixed and redacted current-head proof covers both successful and refused paths.

options.title: Keep actions in the Codex web UI
options.body: Decline the core mutation surface and preserve any reusable read-only discovery work separately.

recommendation.title: Sponsor read-only discovery first
recommendation.body: Land only listing and report extraction now, while deferring mutating action commands until their browser contract and ownership are explicitly accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history-backed owner of Oracle’s browser and CLI foundations.
